gloss: to roll dice; to throw dice

definitions.gloss: to roll dice; to throw dice
definitions.explanation: Used literally in games, and occasionally figuratively to mean taking a chance.

examples.japanese: サイコロを{振|ふ}って{六|ろく}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: I rolled the dice and got a six.

examples.japanese: {順番|じゅんばん}にサイコロを{振|ふ}ってください。
examples.english: Please roll the dice in order.

examples.japanese: すごろくで{遊|あそ}ぶとき、サイコロを{振|ふ}って{出|で}た{数|かず}だけ{進|すす}む。
examples.english: When playing sugoroku, you roll the dice and advance the number shown.

notes:
The standard expression for rolling dice in Japanese. サイコロ (dice) comes from Portuguese (or possibly from {賽|さい}, an older word for dice, combined with コロ suggesting rolling). The verb {振|ふ}る means to shake or swing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サイコロを{二|ふた}つ{振|ふ}る: to roll two dice
- サイコロの{目|め}: the number shown on a die face
- サイコロが{出|で}る: the result comes up
- サイコロ{遊|あそ}び: dice games

RELATED WORDS:
- {賽|さい}は{投|な}げられた: the die is cast (figurative, from Caesar)
- サイコロを{転|ころ}がす: to roll dice (alternative verb)

USAGE:
サイコロ can also be written as {骰子|さいころ} in kanji, though the katakana form is standard. The word {賽|さい} alone can mean dice in more literary contexts.
